transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for making time to discuss the eighth-grade civics oral-history project. As I understand it, the class has proposed having 20 students conduct audio-recorded interviews with community members about local history, using their personal phones, with the recordings published on the public school website and retained indefinitely. Before I can approve this, I need to hear findings from each of you -- the project advisor, counselor, and instructional technology coordinator -- so we can identify any concerns and make sure this plan is sound. Let's start with the project advisor. What are your findings on the proposal?

transcript.text: I've completed the technology review, and I need to flag several critical issues. First, personal phones cannot be used for school recordings. The project must use district tablets instead. Second, the source files must be stored in the restricted OralHistory drive -- not on personal devices or general storage. Third, recordings must be deleted exactly 45 days after the final class presentation; indefinite retention is not permitted. I should note that storing source files in the restricted OralHistory drive does not prohibit publishing consented recordings on the public school website, so that piece can still move forward. Finally, the technology plan must include a secure-storage configuration record documenting these requirements before Dr. Morgan can sign off.
